newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New NZ trans-Tasman cut-price airline planned.
newsitem.headline: New NZ trans-Tasman cut-price airline planned.

text.p: As Hamilton's Kiwi International airline battles for its life, a new cheap fares trans-Tasman venture is planning to take to the sky next week in a copybook imitation of Kiwi's start two years ago, the New Zealand Press Association reported on Wednesday.
Central Pacific Airlines starts once-a-week Auckland-Brisbane charters from Saturday week using an Air Nauru Boeing 737-400.
Kiwi also began its life as a weekly charter airline to Brisbane in 1994 using an Air Nauru Boeing.
Kiwi was in full operation again after a Brisbane court ordered the Singapore operators of its Airbus jet to fly the aircraft after grounding it last weekend over a disputed debt.

Kiwi's public credibility has been dented by the weekend crisis, which followed several weeks of flight disruptions because of environmental and mechanical problems -- some of which Kiwi had no control over.

Air Nauru chief executive Rex Banks said Central Pacific could only lease the jet until the end of October. Qantas wanted to "tie it up" after that -- to stop Air Nauru helping any more new airlines get started, he said.
Central Pacific is owned by a travel agency and is offering fares from NZ$359, said an Auckland spokesman.

The first flight was nearly full and inquiries had been strong from Brisbane and Auckland. Kiwi managing director Patrick Pruett wished the new airline good luck and predicted it would face huge pressure from the major trans-Tasman carriers in Auckland.
He said Kiwi's planned cost-saving service cuts from October 6 cut out its Auckland service, so the new airline was no threat.
Meanwhile, Kiwi's Air New Zealand regional trans-Tasman rival Freedom Air rejected speculation it would pull out of Hamilton if Kiwi failed.
Spokesman Stuart Eastman said a market had been established and if Freedom exited, another trans-Tasman operator would replace it. Freedom's loadings were now 80 percent and more, he said.
Hamilton travel agents said they also believed Freedom would stay.
Air New Zealand chairman Bob Matthew said this week Freedom Air would live on if Kiwi failed.
